_doc: Large batch L03 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): tigers (jungle, elder), black jaguar, leopards (cloud, ghost), lynxes (tufted, snow), mischief monkey, mandrill boss, bearded pig. New motifs live in motifs/large_L03.js (32 motifs, glyph/motion ids prefixed L03-, 8 custom chain effects); reused: snow-bank (L02, the same drift picture). Every piece (unique and class) has a hand note naming its picture, with an explicit motif and layout. All 10 signature motifs are new and used as a signature by no other creature; siblings share only secondary motifs (tiger-stripe/tiger-claw/tiger-leap with the elder tiger in grey, lynx-spring/hook-claw/lynx-tufts with the snow lynx in pale grey, fruit-lob with the bearded pig).

jungle-tiger.notes: Jungle tiger of the forest and rainforest: orange with black stripes, slinking low through dappled leaf shade, freezing, then the pounce; the stripes are both its picture and its hiding place.

u0.n: Stripe Stalk: a striped tiger creeps out low, freezes in the shade and melts back in; you only saw the stripes

u1.n: Tiger Pounce: the tiger crouches, then flies off the edge forepaws first, jungle leaves shaken loose drifting down

u2.n: Rake Claws: a paw runs the edge with its claws out; the scars it leaves darken into black stripes

u3.n: Striped Dash: the stalk breaks into a sprint, a blur of stripes streaking along the edge in a dust trail

b0.n: Stripe-Shade Rake: clawed paws swipe out of the shade, leaving stripe-shaped scars

b1.n: Shade-Pounce Mangle: the tiger leaps out of the shade, lands hard and mauls, dust flying

b2.n: Dappled Stance: broad jungle leaves line the edge, sun flecks blinking through them over the hidden tiger

b3.n: Shade Slip: the leaves shove apart and swing back as the tiger slips through the shade

x0.n: Leaf-Fall Slam: the tiger drops out of the canopy onto the edge in a fall of leaves

elder-tiger.notes: Elder tiger: an old tiger with greying, faded stripes, old scars and huge paws; slower than the jungle tiger, it hits harder, licks its wounds back closed and fakes a limp.

u0.n: Elder Pounce: a huge old paw lifts and slams down, a pale scar across the pad, grey dust bursting

u1.n: Scar Lick: a pink tongue licks along an old stitched scar; the scar shortens and a plus rises

u2.n: Stripe Veil: greying striped flanks push out along the edge like a veil of old stripes and hold

u3.n: Limp Feint: uneven tracks wander out and back, one hind paw dragging: the old tiger fakes a limp

b0.n: Grizzle Swipe: a grey paw swipes, blunt old claws leaving faded stripes

b1.n: Grizzle Mangle: the great paw hammers off the edge again and again in grey dust

b2.n: Grizzle Stance: huge scarred paws plant along the edge and do not move

b3.n: Grizzle Lurch: a lurching, dragged step shoves out and back

x0.n: Grizzle Return: the old tiger leaps once more, greyer and slower, still deadly

black-jaguar.notes: Black jaguar of the rainforest: jet black so that only the yellow eyes show, faint rosettes surfacing in the sheen of the coat; it drops out of the branches in the rain and kills with one crunching bite.

u0.n: Night Lunge: dark jaws lunge along the edge, two white fangs leading, and crunch

u1.n: Shadow Slip: the yellow eyes blink shut and open again somewhere else along the edge

u2.n: Night Coat: faint rosettes surface in the black coat's sheen along the edge, a glint going round each

u3.n: Night Drop: the jaguar drops from above; its jaws fall onto the edge and crunch shut

b0.n: Rosette Rake: rosette marks rake off the edge, glinting in the sheen

b1.n: Downpour Maul: a cloudburst slams down along the edge, splash crowns and puddle rings

b2.n: Rain Crouch: steady rain falls past the edge on the crouched black coat

b3.n: Ledge Leap: the eyes leap out of the dark and back

x0.n: Dark Descent: two yellow eyes drop out of the canopy, blinking

cloud-leopard.notes: Cloud (clouded) leopard of the mountain forests: tawny-grey with big dark-rimmed cloud blotches, a very long thick ringed tail; it hangs from branches and rock ledges and comes and goes like mist.

u0.n: Branch Drop: the claws let go of the ledge and the leopard drops, pebbles flying

u1.n: Cloud Coat: dark-rimmed cloud blotches drift out like clouds and back in a mountain mist

u2.n: Long Tail: the long ringed tail flicks up at one spot, then another, the tip hooking

u3.n: Rumour Step: blotches flicker from spot to spot, faint prints where it may have stepped

b0.n: Ledge-Grip Rake: paws hooked on a rock ledge rake out, white claws over the stone

b1.n: Cloud Rend: blotches tear off the edge like torn cloud

b2.n: Ledge-Hold Stance: big paws grip a stone ledge all along the edge

b3.n: Phantom Ledge Slink: only the long tail slinks out and back along the ledge

x0.n: Ledge Plunge: the leopard plunges off the ledge and slams down, rock dust bursting

ghost-leopard.notes: Ghost leopard of the high mountains: pale grey with faint rosettes, nearly invisible against snow and rock; you see half a rosette in the mist, frost in its fur, and prints in the snow with nothing making them.

u0.n: Fade Out: pale rosettes drift out and fade to a few pixels in the mist, then come back

u1.n: Ice Pelt: frost-stiff fur spikes bristle out, an ice crystal on each tip

u2.n: Phantom Pounce: rosettes flash almost whole for an instant as the unseen cat strikes, snow kicked up

u3.n: Flicker Step: paw prints appear in the snow at one spot, then another, with nothing making them

b0.n: Ghost Flicker: half-drawn rosettes flicker at spot after spot

b1.n: Ghost Strike: frosted claws of fur strike out of the mist

b2.n: Ghost Mist: faint rosettes hang along the edge in the mist

b3.n: Ghost Slip: prints step out across the snow and back, then dither away

x0.n: Ghost Rush: a line of prints races along the edge, no cat to be seen

tufted-lynx.notes: Tufted lynx of the forest and mountain: tawny, white side ruffs, long black ear tufts that twitch, a bobtail, long hind legs for the spring and a hooked claw.

u0.n: Ear Twitch: tufted ears pop out, one tuft flicks, then the other, and they duck back

u1.n: Lynx Spring: a coiled lynx springs off the edge on long hind legs, bobtail up

u2.n: Hook Claw: one long claw runs the edge, curling into a hook as it goes

u3.n: Surprise Pounce: ears shoot up out of the grass and pounce, surprise marks popping

b0.n: Tufted Swipe: a furry paw swipes out, its claw hooking

b1.n: Soft Paw Pin: the lynx springs and pins, landing soft

b2.n: Tuft Crouch: a row of tufted ears crouches along the edge, twitching

b3.n: Sudden Brush: tufted ears brush up at one spot, then another

x0.n: Ear Tuft Pounce: the lynx springs ears first, angry marks popping

snow-lynx.notes: Snow lynx of the mountain and tundra: pale grey, ear tufts, and huge furry snowshoe paws that press and sink, puffing snow; it hides under drifts and drains the warmth out of its prey.

u0.n: Snow Leap: a pale lynx springs off the edge and lands in a burst of snow

u1.n: Paw Snap: huge snowshoe paws snap out, snow puffing sideways from the pads

u2.n: Drift Cover: snowdrifts heap up along the edge over the lynx

u3.n: Snowshoe Glide: the big paws skim out over the snow and back without sinking

b0.n: Lynx Swipe: a pale furry paw swipes, the claw hooking

b1.n: Lynx Drift Pounce: the lynx springs into the drift and pins, snow flying

b2.n: Lynx Snowshoe: wide furry paws stand along the edge, sunk in the snow

b3.n: Lynx Stealth: only the tufted ears show above the drift, at one spot, then another

x0.n: Lynx Dive: the lynx dives head-first into the snow

mischief-monkey.notes: Mischief monkey of the rainforest: brown with a peach face, swings by its tail, steals hats and pockets, throws fruit and pulls faces at you.

u0.n: Pocket Pick: little hands dip in at tied spots and come back with a coin, a key, a red hat

u1.n: Fruit Fling: ripe fruit is lobbed off the edge, spinning, and splats

u2.n: Swing Away: the monkey swings out by its tail and back, just out of reach

u3.n: Grimace: cheeky faces push out pulling grins, tongues and raised eyebrows

b0.n: Hat-Snatch Grab: a quick hand darts out and comes back with a little red hat

b1.n: Tail-Swing Bonk: the monkey swings in by its tail and bonks

b2.n: Cheeky Shrug: a row of cheeky faces along the edge, shrugging and grinning

b3.n: Pocket-Pick Pinch: a hand shoves in and pinches a coin back out

x0.n: Tree-Drop Slam: the monkey lets go of the branch and drops onto the edge

mandrill-boss.notes: Mandrill boss of the troop: red nose ridge, blue ridged cheeks, an orange beard and huge canines; it glares, yawns to show its fangs, drums its chest and charges.

u0.n: Mandrill Charge: the painted face charges off the edge, glaring, dust kicked up

u1.n: Fang Flash: a threat yawn runs the edge, jaws gaping on two huge white canines, a fang flash

u2.n: Chest Beat: fists drum the chest and blue shock arcs pulse out along the edge

u3.n: Face Off: the red and blue face looms right up to you, brows down, nostrils flared

b0.n: Painted Swipe: the painted face sweeps along the edge in red and blue

b1.n: Humourless Grab: the yawn snaps shut on a grab

b2.n: Painted Stance: painted faces glare along the edge

b3.n: Mandrill Troop Shove: fists thump out and shove back

x0.n: Furious Stomp: fists and shock arcs pound off the edge in dust

bearded-pig.notes: Bearded pig of the rainforest and swamp: grey-brown, a long pointed snout and a long pale beard; it ploughs the mud, follows the nut and fruit falls and bristles up its back.

u0.n: Beard Barge: bearded snouts barge off the edge, the long pale beards swinging

u1.n: Mud Plough: the snout ploughs out through the mud, a bow wave ahead and clods flying

u2.n: Nut Shield: winged forest nuts pile up along the edge, nut by nut

u3.n: Fruit Snatch: fallen fruit at one spot after another vanishes as the snout darts at it

b0.n: Bristle Root: the snout roots along the edge, turning the soil over

b1.n: Bristle Plough: the snout ploughs in and heaves the mud up

b2.n: Bristle Shield: a ridge of stiff pale bristles stands up along the edge

b3.n: Bristle Snatch: the bearded snout shoves in and snatches back

x0.n: Bristle Ram: the bristled back rams off the edge, dust flying
